choices: Attacks the source of the assessment rather than its substance
Assumes family connections are always disclosed
Overlooks the colleague's professional record
Relies on an unverified claim about the connections
questions.explanation: This is an ad hominem: the colleague's ties might warrant scrutiny of the analysis, but they establish nothing about whether it is correct. Family connections could as easily be a source of insight as of bias, which is why they cannot substitute for engaging the argument.

questions.stem: The change in survey method matters because:
choices: Differences in mode can shift responses independently of any change in actual trust
Telephone surveys are always less accurate
The sample size may have changed
Respondents may have forgotten the initiative
questions.explanation: Respondents answer sensitive questions differently by telephone than face to face, so any part of the 9-point movement may be an artifact of measurement. The second option overstates it — the problem is that the two waves are not comparable, not that one method is inferior.

questions.stem: The specialist's argument is most vulnerable to the objection that:
choices: The war preceding the organization's founding may explain the subsequent peace
The organization has other functions besides preventing war
Member states have had disputes short of war
The organization's membership has changed over time
questions.explanation: A decisive war that settled the territorial questions removes the principal cause of fighting, so peace may be the legacy of the settlement rather than the achievement of the organization. The final sentence of the stimulus supplies this alternative explanation directly.

questions.stem: Which principle, if accepted, would most undermine the official's proposal?
choices: Programs should be evaluated by what they accomplish rather than by what they cost to administer
Administrative costs should be minimized wherever possible
Grant decisions should be made by technical experts
Donors should support a diverse portfolio of grantees
questions.explanation: The proposal rests entirely on an administrative cost ratio, so a principle subordinating cost to accomplishment removes its only support. The fourth option also cuts against the proposal but on narrower grounds — it would permit concentration if diversity were otherwise satisfied.

questions.stem: Which principle, if accepted, would most support the commentator's conclusion?
choices: A program should be judged a failure unless rigorous evaluation demonstrates a measurable benefit
Programs should be continued until proven harmful
Evaluation methods should be chosen by independent experts
Household income is the best measure of development impact
questions.explanation: The commentator treats the absence of demonstrated effect as sufficient for a verdict of failure, which only a principle placing the burden of proof on the program can license. The second option states the opposite presumption, and the fourth supports the choice of outcome without addressing the burden.

questions.stem: Which principle, if accepted, would most support the official's proposal?
choices: Personnel policies should maximize aggregate career satisfaction even where individual preferences differ
Officers should be consulted before assignment policies change
Hardship posts should receive additional resources
Career satisfaction should be measured annually
questions.explanation: The proposal would compel service that officers might not choose, so it needs a principle permitting aggregate benefit to override individual preference. The second option would obstruct the proposal, and the third and fourth are administrative measures that leave the mandate unjustified.

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the director's conclusion?
choices: Among applicants with identical admission scores, those admitted outperform those turned away
The institute has operated for twenty years
Graduates report high satisfaction with the curriculum
The certification examination is nationally standardized
questions.explanation: Comparing candidates matched on the selection variable removes the admissions advantage, so a remaining gap is attributable to the institute. Satisfaction and program longevity say nothing about whether the instruction caused the performance difference.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best supported by the exchange described?
choices: The surveillance program disrupted no plots
The necessity of the program has not been established by the evidence cited
Conventional methods are always sufficient
The security service acted unlawfully
questions.explanation: The civil liberties group disputes what the four disruptions prove, not that they occurred, so what remains open is necessity. The first, third, and fourth options each assert something neither party has established.

questions.stem: The economic section's argument depends on the assumption that:
choices: Genuine growth in an economy of this kind would show more year-to-year variation
The host government has a motive to misreport
Other economies in the region report lower growth
International organizations have questioned the figures
questions.explanation: The inference runs entirely from implausible smoothness, which requires that real economies of this type fluctuate. Motive and third-party doubts would make the suspicion more compelling but are not what the stated reasoning rests on.

questions.stem: Which of the following must be true if the evaluator's observation is accurate?
choices: Some organizations capable of performing well are excluded from funding by the audit requirement
Audited organizations perform better than unaudited ones
The donor is indifferent to local rootedness
Audit costs exceed the value of small grants
questions.explanation: If the requirement is binding on the smallest and most locally rooted organizations, at least some competent applicants are screened out — this follows directly. The other options add claims about performance, motive, and cost that the observation does not establish.

questions.stem: If both the ministry's figure and the registration figure are accurate, which is best supported?
choices: The campaign had no effect whatsoever
Fatalities per registered vehicle did not fall and may have risen
The fuel price increase was intended as a safety measure
Traffic fatalities will rise again next year
questions.explanation: Registrations fell 22 percent while fatalities fell 18 percent, so the ratio moved unfavorably. The first option overstates the case — a modest campaign effect could still be hidden inside these aggregates, which is exactly why the raw decline proves nothing.
